sections.html:
The median value of owner-occupied homes in Pekin is $120,700, so repair costs can take a large share of the price. A new roof or furnace is a bigger decision when the house is worth that little, and for that reason many sellers weigh a cash purchase against listing and fixing the house first.

Pekin is the county seat of Tazewell County, on the Illinois River in central Illinois. Population was 31,731 in 2020 and is estimated at 31,277 now. A small part of the city lies in Peoria County, so some Pekin addresses are recorded and taxed in a different county than most of the city.

  • Confirm your flood zone and your school district boundary.
  • Ask the title company which county records your parcel and whether any liens or unpaid taxes are on file.
  • Compare offers by what you keep after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not by headline price.

The city takes part in the National Flood Insurance Program, and properties below the 1 percent annual chance flood level may be required by law to carry flood insurance. An owner who thinks the flood designation is wrong can ask FEMA for a Letter of Map Amendment, and lenders may still require insurance. Properties along the Illinois River are often subject to floodway rules.

For a sale, find out your flood zone early, since it affects a buyer's mortgage and insurance. New construction in a flood hazard area must set the lowest floor two feet above base flood elevation.

sections.h2: Permits and yard rules before a sale
sections.html:
Pekin's Inspections Department requires permits for electrical, plumbing, sewer, heating, ventilation and air conditioning work, and also for fences, sheds, new homes, additions, decks, signs and pools. A roofing permit applies to a complete tear-off or a second layer of shingles. Siding, windows, doors and interior remodeling need none unless the work changes structural walls, plumbing or electrical.

Other rules a buyer's agent may bring up:

  • A homeowner may do their own work but must still get a permit. The city defines a homeowner as the person who owns and lives at the residence.
  • Pools deeper than 24 inches need a permit and may sit only in the rear yard.
  • Chain link fences are not allowed in any front yard, and corner lots must keep sight lines clear.
  • Vehicles may not be parked in yards or the right of way, and must stand on a hard surface such as concrete or asphalt.

The Inspections Department takes questions at 309.478.5364. If you built a deck or finished a basement without a permit, ask whether it can be inspected before you list.

sections.h2: Which county records a Pekin deed?
sections.html:
Most Pekin parcels are in Tazewell County, where the County Clerk and Recorder keeps real estate records. Everything in the Recorder's files is public record, anyone may look through it free of charge, and some forms are supplied at no cost. Ask the office for current recording fees and transfer stamp amounts before closing, since they change.

Parcels in the Peoria County portion go through Peoria County instead. Its land records office takes part in the state's MyDec system, which lets filers submit the PTAX-203 transfer declaration electronically before a deed is recorded. Check your tax bill or parcel number to see which county applies, and tell your closing attorney if the house straddles the line.

Coal mining once left its mark under parts of Pekin, though it had ended by 1951. One mine, run by the Pekin Coal Mining Company until 1952, lay under what later became Broadmoor Junior High, Willow Elementary and Schramm School, and another crossed Broadway in the eastern part of town.

If a buyer asks whether your lot sits over old workings, the title company or the county recorder's records are the place to start. Do not guess at the answer in a listing.

Public schools depend on where the house sits. Most of the city is in Pekin Public School District 108. Parts of the Tazewell County side belong instead to North Pekin-Marquette Heights School District 102 or Rankin Community School District 98, and all of Pekin in Tazewell County feeds Pekin Community High School District 303. The Peoria County portion is in Hollis Consolidated School District 328 and Limestone Community High School District 310.

Ask the district for the boundary of your address before a buyer does. CityLink buses on Routes 17, 18 and 23 connect the city to downtown Peoria, which helps buyers who commute.

A listed sale usually brings showings, a buyer's mortgage and appraisal, and a list of repairs after the inspection. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands skips those steps, which suits an older house in a flood zone, a property with permit questions, or one that is vacant or inherited. Compare what you would keep from each route, not just the price on the offer.

faqs.a: Pekin is the county seat of Tazewell County. A small part of the city extends into Peoria County, so parcels there are recorded and taxed through Peoria County. Check your parcel number to see which applies.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Pekin?
faqs.a: Yes, for a complete tear-off and replacement, or for adding a second layer of shingles. Siding, window and door replacement do not need a permit unless structural, plumbing or electrical changes are involved.

faqs.q: Does Pekin have flood rules that affect a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The city takes part in the National Flood Insurance Program, and properties below the 1 percent annual chance flood level may be required by law to carry flood insurance. New construction in a flood hazard area must set the lowest floor two feet above base flood elevation.

faqs.q: Can I do my own repairs on my Pekin house?
faqs.a: Yes, if you own and live in it, but you still need the permit. Nobody may work on someone else's property unless licensed or registered with the Inspections Department.

faqs.q: Where do I get recording information for a Pekin sale?
faqs.a: Ask the Tazewell County Clerk and Recorder, whose office keeps real estate records open to the public at no charge. For the Peoria County portion of the city, use the Peoria County land records office, which accepts the MyDec transfer declaration.
